name: Barren Island Volcano Expedition
experienceType: Offshore Marine Expedition · Volcano Viewing · Snorkelling · Catch & Release Game Fishing

content.description:
The Barren Island Volcano Expedition is a rare offshore journey to India's only active volcano, located deep in the Andaman Sea. This is not your regular sightseeing cruise or a casual island hopping trip. It is a full day marine expedition designed for travellers seeking offbeat, once in a lifetime experiences.

Departing early from Havelock Island, the expedition crosses open waters toward one of India's most isolated geological formations. As the coastline fades, the sea deepens in colour and the volcanic mass rises sharply from the horizon.

Landing on the island is strictly prohibited under Indian law. The experience centres around observing the volcano responsibly from the sea, within permitted marine limits. When sea conditions and visibility allow, guests may snorkel in designated reef zones near volcanic rock formations.

This experience is conducted with strict safety protocols, sustainability practices, and weather based decision making.

faqs.question: Is Barren Island really an active volcano?
faqs.answer: Yes. Barren Island is India's only active volcano and one of the few active volcanoes in South Asia. It has been active since 1787 with recent eruptions recorded in 2025..

faqs.question: Can visitors land on Barren Island?
faqs.answer: No. Landing is strictly prohibited under Indian law. The experience involves viewing the island from the sea only, within the legal maritime perimeter.

faqs.question: Is snorkelling guaranteed?
faqs.answer: Snorkelling is included in the expedition but is subject to sea conditions and visibility at the time of the visit.

faqs.question: Are dolphin sightings guaranteed?
faqs.answer: No. Dolphins are wild animals in their natural habitat. While sightings are common during the journey, they are never guaranteed as we respect wildlife and do not disturb their natural behaviour.

faqs.question: What happens if the expedition is cancelled due to weather?
faqs.answer: Guests may reschedule, convert to an alternative marine experience such as Long Island, or receive a refund for the expedition component. Permit fees are non-refundable if already processed.

faqs.question: What is the difference between the two boat options?
faqs.answer: The Rapid Fire is an open centre console boat (non-AC) suited for those who enjoy a raw, open-sea experience. The Artemis is an AC cabin boat offering more comfort during the long crossing, ideal for those who prefer a sheltered, air-conditioned environment.

faqs.question: Is this experience suitable for children?
faqs.answer: The minimum age is 10 years. This expedition is best suited for adults and older teens comfortable with long sea journeys. Due to the extended duration at sea and physical demands, it may not be ideal for very young children.

faqs.question: What should I bring for the expedition?
faqs.answer: Essential items include: valid Govt. ID, sunscreen, hat, sunglasses, comfortable swimwear, and any personal medications. Recommended items include a waterproof camera, extra clothes, and motion sickness medication if you are prone to sea sickness.

faqs.question: Can the volcano erupt during our visit?
faqs.answer: Barren Island is monitored by geological authorities. We maintain safe distances and follow all safety protocols. In the unlikely event of increased volcanic activity, authorities would restrict access well in advance.

faqs.question: What is the best time of year for this expedition?
faqs.answer: The best conditions are typically between December and May when seas are calmer. However, weather can be unpredictable and departures are always subject to real time sea conditions.

The Long Island Escape is a full-day marine journey from Havelock that cruises through the Ritchie's Archipelago, includes a guaranteed snorkelling session at South Button Island, and concludes with shoreline time at Lalaji Bay on Long Island.

Departing from Havelock Island, this expedition navigates through the waters of the Ritchie's Archipelago — a scattered formation of islands known for their clear channels and largely untouched coastlines.

The first major marine stop is near South Button Island, part of a protected marine zone known for healthy reef systems. A guaranteed snorkelling session is conducted here in designated safe waters.

The day is structured to balance cruising, snorkelling, and beach time without compressing the experience into a rushed itinerary.

content.description:
The PADI Open Water Diver Course is the world's most recognised entry-level scuba certification.

Over three days, participants move through classroom-based knowledge development, confined water skill sessions, and finally four open water dives in the sea under direct instructor supervision.

Havelock Island offers suitable training conditions with warm water, stable reef systems, and manageable current patterns that allow gradual skill progression.

Upon completion, you are certified to dive independently with a buddy within 18 metres, anywhere globally where PADI certification is accepted.

This is a certification course — not a trial dive.

faqs.question: Do I need prior diving experience?
faqs.answer: No. This course is designed for complete beginners. No prior diving experience is required.

faqs.question: Is this different from a discovery or trial dive?
faqs.answer: Yes. This is a full 3-day certification programme, not a one-time assisted dive. Upon completion you receive a globally recognised PADI certification valid for life.

faqs.question: How deep will I dive during the course?
faqs.answer: Up to 18 metres by the end of the course. This is also the maximum certified depth for independent diving as a PADI Open Water Diver.

faqs.question: Is the certification valid outside India?
faqs.answer: Yes. PADI certifications are recognised globally and accepted at dive centres worldwide.

faqs.question: What is the swimming assessment?
faqs.answer: You must complete either a 200-metre continuous swim (any stroke, no time limit) or a 300-metre swim using mask, snorkel, and fins, plus a 10-minute float or tread water. These are mandatory PADI standards required for certification.

faqs.question: Do I need a medical clearance?
faqs.answer: A PADI medical questionnaire must be completed before the course. Certain conditions such as respiratory issues, cardiac conditions, pregnancy, or recent surgeries may require written clearance from a physician.

faqs.question: Can I upgrade after completing this course?
faqs.answer: Yes. The PADI Open Water certification is the foundation for further courses including Advanced Open Water, Rescue Diver, and eventually Divemaster.

faqs.question: How many students are in each batch?
faqs.answer: Typically 2 students per instructor, ensuring close supervision and personalised training throughout the course.

faqs.question: What if sea conditions prevent open water dives?
faqs.answer: If marine conditions prevent scheduled open water dives, sessions will be rescheduled to the next available safe slot. Partial course completion may require rescheduling of remaining dives.

faqs.question: What is the best time of year for the course?
faqs.answer: October to May offers the best visibility and calmest sea conditions for training. The course operates year-round but is subject to real-time sea and visibility conditions.

name: Advanced Open Water Course (PADI Certification)

content.description:
The PADI Advanced Open Water Diver Course is designed to improve your diving skills and expand your depth capabilities.

Unlike Open Water, this course is dive-focused with minimal classroom theory. You complete five adventure dives that expose you to different diving environments and skill sets.

Two dives are mandatory: the Deep Dive (up to 30 metres) and the Underwater Navigation Dive. The remaining three dives are selected based on conditions and instructor discretion.

Havelock Island's reef systems and varied dive sites provide ideal conditions for skill progression.

Upon completion, you are certified to dive up to 30 metres (subject to age restrictions). This is a progression course — not a beginner programme.

name: Discover Scuba Diving (PADI Experience)

content.description:
Discover Scuba Diving (DSD) is designed for individuals who want to try scuba diving without enrolling in a full certification course. No prior experience or certification is required.

The experience begins with a briefing covering basic equipment usage, underwater breathing techniques, equalisation methods, hand signals, and safety procedures.

Participants then complete a confined or shallow water practice session before proceeding to an open water dive under direct instructor supervision.

The maximum depth for Discover Scuba is 12 metres. The instructor remains in close proximity throughout the entire dive.

This is not a certification course. It is an introductory experience — and if you enjoy it, this dive can be credited toward the PADI Open Water Course.

name: Inter Tidal Walk (Guided by Marine Biologist)

content.description:
The intertidal zone is the space between high tide and low tide — a dynamic ecosystem that exists between land and sea.

When the tide recedes at Govind Nagar Beach, exposed reef beds and tide pools reveal marine life that is normally hidden underwater.

Led by a trained naturalist, the walk focuses on understanding tidal cycles, identifying marine species, learning about reef ecology, responsible marine behaviour, and conservation awareness.

The experience is calm, slow-paced, and educational — ideal for families and children who are curious about marine life.

This is an observation-based experience — not a swimming activity.

name: Game Fishing

content.description:
Game fishing in the Andaman Sea is conducted as a responsible offshore sport rather than commercial harvesting.

Departing from Havelock Island, the boat navigates into deeper waters known for seasonal pelagic movement. The experience focuses exclusively on rod fishing and jigging techniques, allowing travellers to engage directly in the skill and discipline of offshore angling.

There is no net fishing involved at any stage. All catches are handled carefully and released back into the sea immediately after documentation. The emphasis remains on experience and technique rather than extraction.

The session includes guidance from experienced crew familiar with local currents, fish movement patterns, and seasonal behaviour. This is a marine activity shaped by natural conditions — success depends on weather, season, and fish movement.

faqs.answer: No. Fishing depends on season, weather, and natural conditions. Success cannot be guaranteed as this is a wild marine environment.

faqs.answer: Recommended for guests aged 12 and above due to the offshore open-sea conditions and the nature of the activity.

faqs.question: What is the difference between half-day and full-day?
faqs.answer: The half-day option runs for 4–5 hours and is well-suited for those with limited time. The full-day option runs for 7–8 hours, covering more offshore ground and allowing an extended active fishing window with higher chances of species encounters.

faqs.question: What is the difference between the two boat options?
faqs.answer: The Rapid Fire is an open centre console boat (non-AC) suited for those who enjoy a raw, open-sea experience. The Artemis is an AC cabin boat offering more comfort during the crossing, ideal for those who prefer a sheltered, air-conditioned environment.

faqs.question: What species can I expect to catch?
faqs.answer: Common seasonal species include Sailfish, Giant Trevally, Barracuda, Kingfish, Red Snapper, Marlin, and Grouper. Species vary by season and cannot be guaranteed.

faqs.question: What happens if weather conditions are unfavourable?
faqs.answer: If sea conditions are deemed unsafe, guests may reschedule, convert to an alternative marine experience (pricing differences applicable), or receive a refund for the activity component. Final decision rests with the captain and maritime authorities.

faqs.question: What is the best season for game fishing in Andaman?
faqs.answer: October to May offers the best conditions, with calmer seas and more predictable fish movement. Departures are always subject to real-time sea conditions.
